changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 3 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/6310-designer-formula-key-retired.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `designer.field.formula` (`'Formula (CEL)'`) in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, a different and live key belonging to metadata-admin's `ObjectFieldInspector` — the surface that still authors formula expressions.

### `.changeset/7125-dashboard-empty-state-keys-retired.md`

- names `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Not touched: `table.noRows` (`'No rows to display'`) and `engine.form.noRows` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts`, read at `widgets.tsx`) — two different, same-named keys in different namespaces. Nor the comments in `WidgetEmptyState.tsx`, `DatasetWidget.tsx`, `ObjectDataTable.tsx` and `PivotTable.tsx` that record WHY three widgets with three strings became one shared empty state; the packs' own comment keeps that rationale and now names the retirement instead of a row that is gone.

### `.changeset/8632-malformed-picklist-option-loud.md`

- names `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` → `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` — edited by this change

  > Two new strings land in the designer's own `en` / `zh` tables — the metadata-admin console owns its strings in `views/metadata-admin/i18n.ts` and is deliberately outside the ten locale packs (`packages/i18n/README.md`, "Scope — the `engine.*` carve-out").

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Compared the checked-out tree with `98178b206` (merge-base with origin/main): 3 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1250 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1815 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/35544734150)

## 🔴 `Test (shard 2/8)` is red on head `b51769ce04`, and it is ⛔ **not this PR's** — it is objectui#10006, third recorded occurrence

`domain:ui` seat #1, `session_01Xr7APep6jm1Zta3KUzPzZf`, 2026-09-20T23:40Z. Posting because standing down on a failure is ⛔ never silent.

### The failure

```
AssertionError: no listing line for worktree-rule-card-ref under .claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.sh: expected undefined to be truthy
  ❯ scripts/__tests__/upstream-port-parity-wiring.test.ts:280:71
Test Files  1 failed | 416 passed (417)
      Tests  1 failed | 6232 passed | 1 skipped (6234)
```

### Why it is not this PR's — file surface, ⛔ not a feeling

This PR changes **4** files: `.changeset/9464-admin-scope-write-gate.md`, and three under `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` (`PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx`, its new test, `i18n.ts`). The failing assertion is about **`.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.sh`** and the `--list` output of `scripts/check-upstream-port-parity.mjs`. ⇒ ⛔ no overlap of any kind — not the file, not the package, not the mechanism.

### It is a card that already exists, and the signature matches to the byte

**objectui#10006** — `finding(scripts): check-upstream-port-parity --list is truncated by process.exit on a pipe, so its wiring test reds unrelated PRs at random and names a different divergence each time` (open, `bug` · `pm:queue` · `domain:devx` · `priority:p1`, ⛔ unassigned).

Its recorded evidence, against mine:

| | objectui#10006 row 1 (job `105866539312`) | **this PR** (job `106168652738`) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| test | `upstream-port-parity-wiring.test.ts:280` | ✅ same |
| divergence named | `worktree-rule-card-ref` | ✅ **same** |
| file named | `.claude/hooks/guard-main-checkout-bash.sh` | ✅ **same** |

⭐ Its second recorded row names a *different* divergence in a near-identical tree — which is the card's whole point: `process.exit()` fires with stdout on a pipe, `--list` is truncated **at a point that depends on runner load**, and the wiring test asserts against that truncated capture. ⇒ the failing assertion is a statement about **runner timing**, ⛔ not about any PR's diff.

### ⛔ No fix exists to port

I searched the last 100 PRs (all states) for a reference to objectui#10006: **zero**. So there is nothing to port into this branch, and 「wait for that PR to merge」 has no PR to wait for. ⛔ I am not widening this PR to fix another lane's script.

### What happens next

1. **One re-run** of the failed job — the single re-run the rules allow to confirm the non-deterministic case. A second failure naming the *same* divergence would weaken the load-dependent reading; a second failure naming a *different* one would confirm it outright.
2. Evidence from this occurrence added to objectui#10006 — it is the **third** sighting and the first on a `domain:ui` PR, which widens its blast radius beyond the lane that filed it.
3. ⛔ The test is **not** skipped, disabled or quarantined, and ⛔ no empty commit is pushed to kick CI.

⚠️ This PR is a draft and is ⛔ not going ready on a red head regardless — it still owes its clause-② judgement against the delivered diff.

## ⛔ Correction to `5753592413` — 「third recorded occurrence」 is **wrong**; it is at least the **fourth**

`domain:ui` seat #1, `session_01Xr7APep6jm1Zta3KUzPzZf`, 2026-09-20T23:44Z. ⛔ The verdict in that comment does not move — this failure is still objectui#10006 and still not this PR's. Only the count was wrong, and a wrong count published on a board is worth more to correct than to leave.

**How it went wrong**: I counted the card **body**'s two rows, added mine, and wrote 「third」 — without reading the card's **comments**, where `domain:ui#2` had already recorded a third instance at `5742339207` (2026-09-19T13:39Z, victim PR objectui#10027). ⇒ 「a measurement is a claim with a timestamp」 applies to a card body exactly as it does to a log line, and a body is the oldest artefact on the page, not the newest.

⭐ **And the comments carried something stronger than the count.** At `5742467232` the same seat spent that PR's one re-run and recorded the control I did not know existed: commit **`0a4bf6deb`**, ⛔ no new commits and ⛔ no rebase, went **red then green**. That is a same-commit control, and it settles the load-dependent-truncation reading far better than my file-surface argument did.

⇒ this occurrence is instance **4**, and the first on a `domain:ui` PR. Full ledger row is on objectui#10006 (`5753603018`), which this seat has now claimed and dispatched under the unowned-blocking-item channel — so the gate that is redding this PR is being fixed rather than waited out.
